claim: For the canonical minimal finite sphere models \(X_3=S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\) and \(X_2=S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\), the compact-open finite mapping space \(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2)\) has exactly \(738\) points and admits \(732\) successive Stong beat-point deletions, with \(128\) up-beat and \(604\) down-beat deletions, leaving exactly the six constant maps. The surviving subspace is canonically order-isomorphic to \(X_2\), has no beat points, and therefore is the core. Hence \(\operatorname{core}(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2))\cong X_2\) and \(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2)\simeq X_2\).
integrity: The finite claim is supported by a complete replayable beat-point certificate. The verifier exhausts every set map before filtering by monotonicity and checks every deletion against the current mapping poset.
scientific_limitations: Exact only for the canonical pair \((X_3,X_2)\); no uniform mapping-space theorem for arbitrary finite sphere models is asserted.
title: The finite mapping space from the minimal three-sphere to the minimal two-sphere has two-sphere core
